faqs.question: What does Single Antigen Bead Assay (Class II) measure?
faqs.answer: The Single Antigen Bead Assay identifies the HLAs (Class II) on the surface of cells.

faqs.question: Why is Single Antigen Bead Assay (Class II) done?
faqs.answer: • To determine donor-recipient compatibility for organ transplantation • To assess the risk of organ rejection after transplantation • To evaluate previous transplant outcomes and identify reasons for rejection • To guide treatment decisions and adjust immunosuppressive therapy • To monitor patients with autoimmune diseases like lupus or rheumatoid arthritis

faqs.question: When is Single Antigen Bead Assay (Class II) recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test is recommended when • a patient requires an organ transplant, • assessing organ compatibility between a donor and recipient, • evaluating risks of rejection after transplantation, • monitoring immunosuppressive therapy effectiveness, or • diagnosing autoimmune diseases like lupus or rheumatoid arthritis.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Single Antigen Bead Assay (Class II) are abnormal?
faqs.answer: If the Single Antigen Bead Assay (Class II) results are abnormal, it may indicate a higher risk of organ rejection or incompatibility between a donor and recipient.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Single Antigen Bead Assay (Class II)?
faqs.answer: A small sample of your blood will be collected. The blood sample will be sent to the laboratory for testing.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Single Antigen Bead Assay (Class II)?
faqs.answer: • No specific dietary restrictions are necessary. • Inform your doctor about any medications you are taking and any specific requirements you have. • Provide a complete medical history to aid in result interpretation.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with Single Antigen Bead Assay (Class II)?
faqs.answer: • Crossmatching: To confirm compatibility between the donor and recipient. • HLA antibody testing: To identify antibodies that may increase the risk of organ rejection. • Tissue typing: Determining tissue compatibility between a donor and recipient for transplantation.

faqs.question: What is the Single Antigen Bead Assay (Class II) also known as?
What is organ transplantation?
faqs.answer: Organ transplantation is a surgical procedure where a healthy organ or tissue is surgically transplanted from a donor into a recipient's body to replace a damaged or non-functioning organ. It is commonly done for conditions such as end-stage renal disease, liver failure, heart failure, or lung disease.
